 Order

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that he has paid Deficit Court Fee vide I.A.No.6291/2023 and Covering Memo No.2472/2023, and in support of the said submission, he has filed a copy of Online Court Fee Cyber Receipt along with the covering memo, therefore, the Court fee may be taken on record.
On due consideration, the Deficit Court Fee is taken on record.

This appeal is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved of award dated 30.08.2017,
passed by learned X Addl. Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal (M.P.), in Motor Claim Case No.1078/2016, on the ground that Tribunal erred in considering the income of the deceased Rambilas at Rs.6400/-, whereas, admittedly Rambilas was working as an Accountant in Bansal Extraction & Export Pvt. Ltd., therefore, at least minimum wages for a skilled labourer should have been taken into consideration which were to the tune of Rs.9085/- on the date of the accident.

entities.text: X Addl. Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2 . It is submitted that there are four dependents on the deceased and, therefore, 1/4th deduction will be made towards the living expenses of the deceased and, thereafter, adding 40% towards future prospects, appropriate compensation is to be computed.
3.
Shri Rohit Jain, opposes the prayer and supports the award.

4. After going through the award, it is evident that when minimum wages are taken into consideration, then income of the deceased can be presumed to be Rs.9085/- if not 10,100/- as was canvassed before the Tribunal and then annual income will come out to Rs.1,09,020/- .

When 1/4th is deducted towards the living expenses of the deceased, then it comes out to Rs.27,255/-.
5.
Thus, the net annual dependency of the family comes out to Rs.81,765/-.
In this amount, 40% is to be added towards the future prospects in the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

2 29 years, multiplier of 17 will be applicable, taking total pecuniary compensation to Rs.19,46,07/-,
(Rupees Nineteen Lacs, Forty Six Thousand and Seven), over and above which claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.70,000/-(Rupees Seventy Thousand) under the head of non-pecuniary compensation and two of the children of the deceased are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand) each towards the loss of parental consortium, taking total compensation to Rs.20,96,007/-.

Besides this, Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh)
towards the medical expenses which when added, then total compensation will come out to Rs.21,96,007/- (Rupees Twenty One Lacs, Ninety Six Thousand and Seven) against a sum of Rs.11,48,164/- (Rupees Eleven Lacs, Forty Eight Thousand, One Hundred and Sixty Four) awarded by learned Claims Tribunal.
6. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.10,47,843/- (Rupees Ten Lacs, Forty Seven Thousand, Eight Hundred and Forty Three) to which claimants will be entitled to.
This additional amount will carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual payment.

It is further directed that this additional amount shall remain invested in a monthly income of an Indian Post Office/Nationalized Bank, as the case may be, for a period of ten years for younger child Bhumi when she attains the age of majority.
Claimants will be entitled to use interest so derived for their upkeep and well being, but they will keep the principal amount intact.
7. In above terms, appeal is disposed off.
8. Let record of Claims Tribunal be sent back.

(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE A.Praj.
